salesLanguage.headline: TX-70-4K: gets the signal from one place to another without moving the equipment
salesLanguage.plainEnglishSummary: Use this when the source, display, USB device or control point is too far away for a simple local cable.
salesLanguage.customerValue: It lets the room be built around where people and displays need to be, rather than where short cables happen to reach.
salesLanguage.realWorldApplication: Displays away from the rack, lecterns, teaching rooms, meeting rooms and point-to-point signal paths.
salesLanguage.salespersonCue: Start with distance and what has to travel: video only, video plus USB, audio, control or network.
talkTrack: It solves a distance problem.
Use it when the video path needs reliable point-to-point extension.
It is usually simpler than AV-over-IP when the path is one source to one display.
discoveryPrompts: How far is the source from the display or USB device?
What signals need to travel over the same path?
Is this a single fixed route or does it need to switch between many destinations?
avoidPositioningAs: Do not use an extender as a routing system when many sources and many displays need flexible switching.
marketApplications: Long-distance video, USB, control and network transport

systemIntegrator.label: SI / installer
systemIntegrator.headline: TX-70-4K: deployment and commissioning view
systemIntegrator.pitch: Use this view when the installer needs to prove the point-to-point route, cable distance, signal direction, power method and USB behaviour if USB is involved.
systemIntegrator.value: Turns the sales conversation into practical install checks: location, cabling, signal direction, dependencies, control and commissioning risk.
talkTrack: Check the practical signal path around HDBaseT, HDMI before finalising the design.
Confirm what connects locally, what leaves the room, and which accessories or endpoints are required.
Check USB class, power method, control path and firmware notes before treating the product as a like-for-like substitute.
discoveryPrompts: Where will the product physically live: table, wall, display, rack, lectern or network closet?
What cable type, distance and route are available between each endpoint?
Which products, receivers, USB devices, controllers or network switches must be present for this to work?
How far is the source from the display or USB device?
What signals need to travel over the same path?
positioningNotes: Good installer language should make dependencies visible before a quote is issued.
Call out install risk early when the product depends on USB bandwidth, network design, endpoint pairing or control integration.
avoidPositioningAs: Do not imply it is plug-and-play where cable distance, USB class, endpoint compatibility, network design or control programming still needs validation.
Do not use an extender as a routing system when many sources and many displays need flexible switching.

consultant.label: Consultant / technical
consultant.headline: TX-70-4K: architecture fit and trade-off view
consultant.pitch: Use this view to decide whether the project is simply a defined distance problem or whether routing, switching or networked AV is actually required.
consultant.value: Helps separate a technically possible product choice from the strongest design choice for the application, budget, risk and future expansion.
talkTrack: Validate the application first, then decide whether this product family is the cleanest architecture.
Compare against simpler or more scalable alternatives where the requirement is fixed, expandable, distance-led or conferencing-led.
Use the specification as evidence after the room workflow and signal architecture are clear.
discoveryPrompts: Is this requirement driven by user experience, source/display routing, distance, USB, collaboration, network distribution, processing or control?
What would make this product the wrong choice even if it technically works?
Is the system expected to grow, change rooms, add endpoints, record, stream or integrate with a wider AV platform?
How far is the source from the display or USB device?
What signals need to travel over the same path?
positioningNotes: Use for architectural judgement, product-family selection and proposal-safe trade-off language.
Be explicit when the product is technically possible but unlikely to be the most natural choice.
avoidPositioningAs: Do not let a feature match override the real application, architecture or operational requirement.
Do not use an extender as a routing system when many sources and many displays need flexible switching.
